title: Canonical exchange and coefficient law predicates
statement: For the recorded six-functor coefficient datum and Cartesian scheme squares, define the exchange law predicates to be the naturality, identity, horizontal/vertical pasting, smooth and proper invertibility, mate and scalar-compatibility equations for the canonical exchange arrows. The finite-stage predicate at $A_{E,n}$, $n\ge1$, conjoins finite naturality, ordinary exchange, support exchange, module smooth and pro-etale smooth laws. Datum identification compares its literal finite arrows to the transported actual pro-etale arrows, and compact identification compares their etale and pro-etale compact-support maps. Completed ordinary/support laws concern the recorded adic datum; completed support naturality, completed mates and square naturality use its actual Roos-limit exchange. Rational and common-stage laws use localization and common-field representatives. Scalar compatibility includes quotient, integral reduction and field extension. All predicates keep their original square domains and hypotheses; this definition asserts no exchange theorem. The constituent notions are [def-fix-six-functor-datum] [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] [def-exchange-projection] [def-cbc-exchange-map] [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].
